proof.criterion: The branch builds a daemon that migrates its database (the tester's round-24 failure)
proof.surface: the daemon's store package and the property model at the merge head, which now carries main's timestamp-aware migration loader
proof.command: cd packages/daemon && env -u LEGION_WORKSPACE -u OMP_SESSION_SQL_DSN_FILE LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=<own Postgres on the issue volume> LEGION_TEST_NATS_URL=nats://127.0.0.1:54222 LEGION_TEST_NATS_MONITOR_URL=http://127.0.0.1:58222 go test -count=1 ./internal/store/... ./internal/record/ ./internal/supervise/
proof.observed: Merge bc514a0d84a0dd5a4b5c2071f8b9ed912b786755 (jj new legion/INFRA-251 main, main 6b1524cdb8aa, no conflict). store 215s ok (TestMigrateAppliesEveryEmbeddedMigration among them), store/migrations ok, record ok, supervise ok; the property model's seeds migrate and run. Changed lines of the branch diff are identical before and after the merge (sha256 of the +/- lines 3fd71f3b41125e75 both sides; 78 files, 12233 insertions, 259 deletions both sides).
proof.negativeControl: At the tester's d90356ab (the renamed migrations without main's loader) TestMigrateAppliesEveryEmbeddedMigration fails: 'unable to encode 20261101163106 into binary format for int4' (tester's evidence).

proof.criterion: The property oracle accepts a second telling exactly when the first catch-up's own telling write failed (or its task was taken back), citing the ruling, and every other double telling stays a failure; seed 41 is pinned and passes
proof.command: cd packages/daemon && env -u LEGION_WORKSPACE -u OMP_SESSION_SQL_DSN_FILE LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=<own Postgres on the issue volume> LEGION_TEST_NATS_URL=nats://127.0.0.1:54222 LEGION_TEST_NATS_MONITOR_URL=http://127.0.0.1:58222 go test -count=1 -run '^TestKeptDecisionsRegressionSeeds$' ./internal/daemon/ ; LEGION_KEPT_PROPERTY_RUNS=150 LEGION_KEPT_PROPERTY_STEPS=300 go test -run '^TestKeptDecisionsReachTheCurrentArchitectOnce$' ./internal/daemon/
proof.observed: Pinned seeds 39 of 39 pass, seed-41-at-300-steps among them (4.12 s). 150 seeds x 300 steps pass. A throwaway driver of tell() (deleted) showed: failed catch-up 112 then catch-up 115 accepted; the same with the write not failed rejected 'told 2 times'; failed 112 and 115 then 118 rejected 'told 3 times'; prompt then non-retold prompt rejected; prompt then retold prompt accepted; failed catch-up then a retold prompt rejected; a telling to another tree's architect unaffected. The tester's seed-41 trace (row 112's forget errored at step 288, row 115 named ask-0015 at step 304) matches the case the oracle now accepts.
proof.negativeControl: With tellingFailed forced false, the throwaway driver's accept case fails 'ask-0015 was told 2 times'. Seed 41 itself did not reproduce on this pod in 50 runs (25 at 100 steps, 25 at 300) nor in a 150x300 sweep under the old oracle: it reaches the case only on some schedules, as the tester's single failure in 150 did.

deviations: Seed 41's failure is schedule-dependent and did not recur here, so its pin proves the run passes, not that it reaches the failed write each time; the oracle's accept and reject cases were exercised directly by a throwaway driver instead.
openQuestions: In the four daemon packages run together on this pod, the only failures were environmental: dropping a test database ('permission denied to terminate process', SQLSTATE 42501), no rootless Docker, gVisor's empty SigIgn, and NATS streams shared between packages run in parallel.
